title: Complete topological group torsors on a normal scheme
statement:
Let $X$ be a nonempty connected normal Noetherian scheme with a geometric point $x$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-geometric-point]; Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact, and normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Put $\Pi_x=\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(X,x)$ [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Let $G$ be a Hausdorff topological group with a basis of identity neighborhoods consisting of open subgroups. Assume either that $G$ is compact or that $G$ is complete for its two-sided uniformity (a net Cauchy for both differences $g_i^{-1}g_j$ and $g_ig_j^{-1}$ converges).

On $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] let $F_G(U)=C(|U|,G)$ with pointwise group law. An $F_G$-torsor means a sheaf of sets $P$ with a right $F_G$-action which is, on a pro-etale covering family, equivariantly isomorphic to the regular right $F_G$-sheaf. Its fibre at $x$ here means the set of sections of its pullback to the spectrum of the algebraically closed field defining $x$; this is a nonempty right $G$-torsor. There is an equivalence between the groupoid of $F_G$-torsors and the groupoid of continuous homomorphisms $\Pi_x\to G$, whose arrows are conjugating elements of $G$. Choosing a point of the fibre specifies the homomorphism rather than just its conjugacy class: changing the point conjugates it. Equivalently, pointed torsors correspond to actual continuous homomorphisms. A homomorphism $\rho$ determines the torsor whose monodromy on its fibre is $\rho$.

This correspondence is natural for pullback along pointed morphisms between schemes with these hypotheses, and for extension of the structural group along continuous homomorphisms $G\to H$ whenever $H$ also satisfies the stated group hypotheses. The pullback representation is composition with the map of etale fundamental groups; extension of structural group is composition with $G\to H$, with the induced point of the fibre. In particular it applies to spectra of fields, where the homomorphism is the Galois descent cocycle: let $X=\operatorname{Spec}k$ for a field $k$, let $x$ be given by an algebraically closed field containing a separable closure $k^s$ [def-pd-separable-closure], and identify $\Pi_x$ with $G_k=\operatorname{Aut}_k(k^s)$. Restriction identifies the fibre of $P$ at $x$ with $P(\operatorname{Spec}k^s)$. For $p$ in it, identify $\operatorname{Spec}k^s\times_k\operatorname{Spec}k^s$ with $\operatorname{Spec}k^s\times G_k$ as in [lem-sfb-field-separable-cech-coordinates], so that $F_G$ of it is $C(G_k,G)$, and write $\mathrm{pr}_2^*p=\mathrm{pr}_1^*p\cdot c$ with $c\in C(G_k,G)$. Then $c$ is the continuous homomorphism attached to the pointed torsor $(P,p)$, with the cocycle convention $c(gh)=c(g)c(h)$ of that node. All groups and sheaves are taken in compatible universes.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.5 (complete groups with open subgroup basis are Noohi), Theorem 7.2.5, Lemmas 7.3.9, 7.4.1 and 7.4.10, pp. 63–71; agent formulation of their torsor consequence using the pushout-to-discrete-G-sets argument in the proof of Lemma 7.4.7. Compact case also Example 7.1.6. No local-field hypothesis is asserted for G.
